author: Tynvale
body:
During the explanation I am going to refer to real life scenarios to hopefully make it easier to understand. I wanted to try to think of a new system because as a lot of people know the staff are going quite fast, and whether it's a demotion or someone retiring it doesn't really matter. I personally think that some new system needs to be implemented and even trialed to help improve the staff as a whole. So here's the idea...

Lets say that Avicus is a business, these would be the roles:
- Admins would be Managers
- Sr Mods would be the Experienced Workers
- Mods would be the majority of the workplace as Workers
- Players would be the customers

If someone were to run this business they would need to assign certain roles to certain workers. But on Avicus it seems like it's the opposite, from what I have seen and experienced the staff hardly get any training and don't get told specific roles to that certain person. They are just expected to know and do what is set. And just like a business if you don't do it up to standards you will be fired/demoted. This is fine and all but you will eventually run into problems like the ones we a currently having.

One way I think it could be fixed is by opening up spots for certain roles. these roles could be things such as:
- Community Manager (talk regularly to community and make sure that there suggestions are being heard)
- Social Manager (organise and control the Avicus social media pages)
- Communications Manager (regular update everyone on things being planned/organised)
And many others roles...

These roles could be applied for just like Mod applications by members of the community and even existing mods. I think that if this was to be implemented it would have to be up to the existing staff to decide if that is your main role or if it is extra work from being a regular staff member. No matter their decision on the roles, every staff member needs professionally treated training.

Some pros of this system are:
- Everything will look much more professional and organised
- Mods won't "compete" against eachother and they will have their own little jobs.
- Allows the work flow and communication of staff to improve
- Involves the community more with roles such as a Community Manager 

Some cons of this system are:
- Will probably need 1-3 people on one role because of timezone issues
- Might end up having lots of staff because of so many different roles, causing the server to have way too much staff

I also think that if this was to be implemented it would show either as it's own rank or they keep the Mod tag but on the staff page their role is shown. Again this is all up to the staff to decide. So that's my idea, I would love to hear some feedback on it, more pros and cons and just some general conversation about some other ideas to help the staff system.

replies.author: FrozenThorn
replies.body:
In my opinion, I think this is a really, really good idea! I really like the idea of all the Mods having their own jobs instead of them all competing; from my short time on the staff team I know what it was like, especially with reports - it meant that sometimes some people could not show their full potential because they couldn't get to reports quickly enough because someone else took it before them! 

I also really love the idea of training. I think that it would be a great opportunity for Mods to train the Jr Mods because it means that the Jr Mods know what to look for and know what to do and the Mods also have a fresh reminder in their heads about hacks and how to spot/deal with a hacker. However, I think that Jr Mods should have a good idea about what hacks are out there and how to spot them. I think it would be a great idea if there was a separate sort of part of the forums for people who would like to be Mods and Jr Mods where there they could go and watch YT videos or read about hacks and what to do in certain situations, it would mean everyone could have a chance to become a Mod and would know what to look for if someone is hacking.

Admins used to have specific roles assigned to them.
We always specifically had a Community Admin and a Staff Admin.

When Tel left though, it was decided that all the Admins would be in a "General Admin" role.

Bringing the Community and Staff Admin back would be a good thing because each Admin would specifically be focused on one thing. This could also increase communication between staff and the community and staff and other staff.
